_note: Fixed development regression suite. Cases 1-10 = application scenarios, 11-13 = Scientific Resolver / 3B. target `kind`: system_specific = literature about the named system itself (flat route may legitimately find it); cross_system = literature about a RELATED system that only the 3B route is meant to surface -- a cross_system target only counts as a 3B contribution if it is in transfer_papers with 3B categories (in_3b), never if only the flat route found it. Case 13 (challenging 3B case) defined 2026-10-06: the query names no protein, only a generic structural feature (~200-residue beta-helical protein); all three targets are cross_system, so recall can only come from the Scientific Resolver (3B) discovering related systems.

cases.query: I want to study whether a folded domain can unfold or refold inside a biomolecular condensate. What coarse-grained approaches could capture both folding and condensate interactions?

I want to simulate a multienzyme metabolic pathway where the enzymes can associate dynamically, and test whether spatial organization changes reaction efficiency. What coarse-grained approaches can couple enzyme organization with reaction kinetics?
I want to simulate how metabolic cofactors partition into a protein condensate and affect enzyme organization. Are there residue-level CG models that can include small cofactors?
I want to model internal organization and morphology of multiphase protein-RNA condensates, not just whether they phase separate. What CG approaches could do this?

I want to model mesoscale organization of thousands of multidomain proteins, beyond the scale accessible to residue-level CG. What approaches can bridge molecular interactions to mesoscale aggregation?
I want to study how a liquid protein condensate gradually hardens through inter-protein beta-sheet formation. What CG approaches can capture both phase separation and structural ageing?
I want to predict sequence-specific protein-DNA recognition and binding affinities while retaining a simulation-based physical model. What CG approaches could be suitable?
I need to simulate a large glycoprotein where glycan flexibility and glycan-protein recognition matter. What CG force fields can explicitly represent protein glycosylation?
